claims.text: The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ('Output value errors') exists and covers symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.

Pulumi emits placeholder text like `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` when an Output<T> is converted to a string in a log line, generated file, or resource property instead of yielding the value.
A Pulumi docs troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading an output value like a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying, branching on, or reading an Output value as if it were a plain value causes errors.
Pulumi Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when another update is in progress.
On Apple Silicon, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi CLI supports `--target` and `--exclude` flags to limit operations to specific resources.
In Pulumi, converting an Output to a string directly (concatenation, logging) does not raise an error by default; it silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In Pulumi TypeScript, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In Pulumi TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Pulumi Python, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported` and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Pulumi Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`; `Output.json_dumps()` should be used instead.
In Pulumi Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error.
In Pulumi C#, converting an Output to a string yields text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.
Setting environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes Output string conversion throw an exception instead of returning placeholder text.

String-composition helpers: `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
An `apply` callback runs asynchronously after the Output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values; a resource's logical name cannot be an Output.
In dynamically typed languages, an `if` on a Pulumi Output is generally always true; in statically typed languages it is usually a compile error.
Values known at program start, such as stack config read with `pulumi.Config`, are plain values and can be branched on normally.
Passing an Output as a resource logical name or loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.

In Pulumi Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`, and `range(some_output)` raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using a Pulumi Output as a dictionary key does not raise; it silently keys on the Output object itself.
Pulumi has no supported way to synchronously block and read a resolved value from an Output.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the update result (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
Linked docs exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/, /apply/, /all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
